title: If we want them to do Knowledge Work, design them as Knowledge Agents — Benjamin Clavié, Mixedbread
talk_summary: Clavié argues agents doing non-code knowledge work should be architected like human knowledge organizations: a lead agent decomposes an open-ended request into sub-queries, searcher sub-agents retrieve and return memos, and the lead synthesizes. He shows tool quality and orchestration each independently move accuracy, and that optimized tools cut tool calls ~20% (≈5x cheaper than unoptimized baseline).

takeaways.technique: Orchestrator + searcher sub-agents with memo handoff
takeaways.what_they_do: The main agent does not search itself; it decomposes the question into aspect queries, dispatches searcher agents that return short memos, then answers from those memos — mirroring a partner/assistant law-firm structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're not going to like search yourself. Just please break down the problem for me. Please write queries about the aspects
takeaways.numbers: +3.5 accuracy points; oracle gap 10→6 points (~40% reduction in mistakes)

takeaways.technique: Optimize retrieval/tool baselines before swapping models
takeaways.what_they_do: They show an unoptimized BM25 baseline is near-useless (~60%) while an optimized one reaches 70-80%, and the best harness hits 90.2% with 20% fewer tool calls — i.e., tuning the tool, not the model, is the lever.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You reach it with 20% fewer tool calls. And that's huge because in practice that's 20% fewer tokens
takeaways.numbers: 90.2% accuracy at 20% fewer tool calls; ~5% of the unoptimized baseline's spend

takeaways.technique: Expose multiple retrieval primitives and teach agents when to use each
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents default to grep/BM25-style queries because that dominates training data, even when semantic search over PDFs is needed; the fix is giving agents several primitives (lexical, semantic, multimodal) and making the harness/model aware of the choice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents will try to write grape queries because grapes everywhere in the training data... that's not always what you need

takeaways.what_they_do: Searchers return a compact memo rather than raw documents, so the orchestrator's context holds conclusions, not source dumps — explicitly framed as context being a finite, costly resource.
takeaways.evidence_quote: context is a finite resource... that's going to cost you a lot of money and b that's still nothing

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure the gap between performance with perfect inputs (oracle) and with the actual system, and track how architecture changes shrink that gap — a cleaner signal than raw accuracy.

Coding agents get pre-scoped tickets; real knowledge work arrives open-ended, so the lead agent must first break the problem into aspects and only then dispatch work — the decomposition step is where quality is won or lost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you've got a client that's got a very open-ended problem and you need to break it down yourself and your agent needs to break it down itself
